cohort: The study included nulliparous women who underwent either vacuum-assisted vaginal deliveries or spontaneous vaginal deliveries at a tertiary research hospital between October 2018 and October 2022.
finding: Vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery was associated with a higher prevalence of caput succedaneum and lower 1st and 5th minute APGAR scores compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery, with no significant differences in other severe maternal or neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery, as a mode of birth, showed an increased risk for caput succedaneum and lower initial APGAR scores but similar rates of other severe maternal and neonatal complications when compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
